intro: If you work as a contractor or freelancer, you may have found that a client wants proof of cover before they'll sign you up, or that you simply want protection if something goes wrong on a job. Searching for contractor insurance near me suggests you'd like to speak to someone local who understands the covers contractors typically need. We can introduce you to a UK insurance broker who will talk through your situation and quote you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for contractor insurance usually need
need_lead: Contractors come to this search with a few common situations in mind.
needs: You've been asked by a client to show professional indemnity cover before a contract can start.
You want public liability cover in place in case your work affects a client's premises or a member of the public.
You're worried about how IR35 rules might affect you and want to understand what insurance is available to help.
You've finished a contract and need to check whether run-off cover is needed for work you've already completed.
You're not sure which covers apply to your trade and want a broker to explain the options before you commit.
context_heading: Who you're dealing with when you buy contractor cover
context: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. Many brokers belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association, and some hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

A broker must understand your demands and needs, explain the key policy features and exclusions, and tell you how they are paid. If a complaint isn't resolved, it can go to the Financial Ombudsman Service. iComply itself isn't regulated and doesn't give advice or provide the insurance; we simply introduce you to a broker who quotes you directly.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of contracting work you do, including your trade or profession and the sector you work in.
Say which covers you've been asked for, such as professional indemnity or public liability, and who is asking.
Mention whether IR35 is a concern for you so the broker knows to discuss the cover available.
Explain whether you've had cover before and whether you need run-off cover for past work.
Give your location, since you searched for contractor insurance near me and may prefer a broker you can speak to locally.
Note any deadline from a client for providing proof of cover, so the broker understands your timing.
questions: Which covers do you think my type of contracting work actually needs, and why?
Will the policy meet the professional indemnity requirement my client has set?
How does IR35 insurance work, and is it included or separate from the rest of the cover?
What run-off cover applies if I stop contracting or change direction, and how long does it last?
What are the main exclusions on this policy that could affect my work?
How are you paid for arranging this cover, and will that be explained to me in writing?

faqs.q: Do I need contractor insurance if my client hasn't asked for it?
faqs.a: Not every contractor is required to hold cover, but some clients make professional indemnity a condition of the contract. A broker can explain what's typical for your trade and let you decide what's right for you.

faqs.q: What is run-off cover and why does it matter?
faqs.a: Run-off cover keeps protection in place for work you've already completed after a policy ends, which can matter if a claim is made later. It's worth asking the broker whether it's included and how it applies to your contracts.

faqs.q: Can a broker help me understand IR35 insurance?
faqs.a: IR35 insurance is available, and a broker can explain what it covers and whether it suits your situation. They can talk through the options alongside your other contractor covers.

faqs.q: How do I check that a broker is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Insurance brokers and intermediaries in the UK must be authorised by the FCA, or be appointed representatives of an authorised firm, and you can check them on the FCA register. You can also ask whether they belong to the British Insurance Brokers' Association or hold Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute.

extra_heading: Choosing a broker you can actually reach
extra: Searching for contractor insurance near me often means you'd rather deal with someone you could meet or phone at short notice, especially when a client is waiting on proof of cover. Distance is only part of it, though: what matters most is whether the broker regularly handles cover for contractors in your trade and can explain the policies in plain terms.

When you compare brokers, ask each one the same set of questions so you can weigh the answers side by side. Find out which covers they'd suggest for your work, what the main exclusions are, whether run-off cover is included, and how they are paid. A broker who answers clearly and puts things in writing is easier to judge than one who only talks in headlines.

It also helps to think about how you'd get in touch if something went wrong mid-contract, and whether the broker handles claims themselves or passes you to the insurer. Ask how they prefer to be contacted and what happens outside normal hours. That practical side of the relationship can matter as much as the quote itself.
Remember that iComply isn't regulated and doesn't give advice or arrange cover; we introduce you to a UK insurance broker who quotes you directly, with the price on application.

extra_faqs.q: Does a broker need to be near me to arrange contractor insurance?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Much of the work can be done by phone, email or video, so a broker further away who specialises in contractor cover may suit you better than a local one who doesn't. If meeting in person matters to you, say so when you enquire and we can take that into account.

extra_faqs.q: What should I have ready before I speak to a broker?
extra_faqs.a: It helps to know the type of contracting work you do, which covers a client has asked for, and any deadline you're working to. Having details of past cover and any claims history to hand will also make the first conversation more useful.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to more than one broker before deciding?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. Nothing stops you from approaching several brokers and comparing what they suggest, how they explain the cover and how they are paid. That gives you a clearer picture before you commit to anything.
